hypothesis: The registry's rlm_spawn_replacement_concurrent_spawns class (warm ~12.5% connect-budget exhaustion on the 4-launch e2e storm, failing EXACTLY at the ~90s budget, machine-independent, CI-green) is not a budget/resource/serialization problem: the port's connect_worker installs the resident's routable command channel BEFORE the worker auth handshake, so a supervisor route that fires in the install-to-auth window (the observed producer: the registration handler's own roster refresh, handle_worker_register -> refresh_roster_entry -> get_state) rides the same unauthenticated connection, the worker answers the non-worker_auth FIRST command with the auth refusal and CLOSES it, and the queued handshake never answers - the launch burns its whole connect budget from a fully-healthy, fully-booted worker. The wait is permanent at ANY budget (the reader pump resolves nothing on EOF), so the 30s unix product default fires it too.
approach: Characterization first (fresh VM m5acphnyyyhygzz7jg2jf957, folded head 8c0ab98b0, the env-gated us launch-trace build b3c493a34 + a scratch storm driver): stage A = 24x the unmodified e2e with FULL panic capture -> 3/24 at exactly 90.06/90.07/90.08s, identical worker-side signature (full boot chain -> bound -> probe accepted (normal probe EPIPE) -> real connection accepted -> NO auth ever received -> a late get_state); stage B = the N-sweep storm driver (independent connections per create, the link's real shape; CLIENT_DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY=64 dispatch) -> N=1/2/4 clean (88-612ms/launch, 0 wedges/112 storms; the e2e's rlm-admission load widens the race window), N=8 fired once (1/16, c2 at exactly 90040ms while 7 siblings took 391ms) with the supervisor-side trace: probe-ok attempts=1 -> connect-ok -> auth-enter budget~89.9s -> 90s silence -> auth-budget-out -> launch-fail phase=connect-auth; the 200ms sampler: load max 2.34/8 vCPU, fork spikes 149/200ms, up to 20 concurrent worker processes (the e2e loop's 15s orphan window) - a scheduling race, not resources. FIX (TS pendingClient/client boundary restored): connect_worker rides the auth on a PRIVATE channel clone (route_command_on/route_command_on_typed - the same admission/enqueue/reply machinery, the channel as a parameter); install_command_channel(epoch, channel) installs for routing ONLY after the auth answer, epoch-guarded; pre-auth routes fail fast with the retryable not-connected error (the registration refresh skips - a failed refresh was already its no-op; route_command_ready retries until install; the rebind seam keeps the launch path; the update-snapshot treats mid-handshake as not-collectible). Oracles: handshake_channel_stays_private_until_auth_answers (a hand-driven fake worker socket drives the REAL connect_worker: mid-handshake cmd_tx None -> the answer -> installed) + a_mid_handshake_registration_cannot_kill_the_handshake (the deterministic forced interleave: registration mid-handshake, the wire must carry EXACTLY the auth frame, the handshake completes; RED pre-fix / GREEN post-fix).
parity_notes: TS's connectWorker holds the handshake client PRIVATELY (worker.pendingClient) and installs the routable handle (worker.client = client) ONLY AFTER authenticateWorker answers; TS has no registration-pull (the worker PUSHES its roster snapshot right after auth). The port's pre-auth channel install was the divergence that created the wedge; the fix restores the TS boundary at the port's channel seam. The launch budget constants are untouched (30s unix default, the 90s test override, the 10s auth floor, the probe/backoff grid); no frozen surface changes (no wire, schema, prompt, TUI, or session-JSONL bytes touched - the supervisor's internal channel ownership only).
